paragraphs.text: Analysis returns one nested value. Each level owns the level below it and carries its own data.

Paragraph.text is the text the parser reads, a markdown paragraph's inline markup removed. Sentence.text is rebuilt from the tokens, so its spacing can differ from the source. Both are normalized, and each carries a span, in UTF-8 bytes, saying where in the analysed text it came from. Each paragraph that is not a quote is parsed on its own, so a sentence always belongs to exactly one paragraph, rather than being matched back by text.

Inside a sentence, exactly one token has head equal to 0: the root. Every other token names its governor in head and the relation in dep. Those two columns are what turn a flat token list into a tree.
Words keep their reading order left to right; height is depth in the tree. built is the root, everything else hangs off it directly or through one more hop, so its tree_depth is 2.

The same two columns, read from matra's output for five short sentences. The table is what a Sentence holds; the arcs below it draw each head and dep. The first sentence carries a negation, the second a modal, the third a clausal complement, the fourth a root adverbial, and the fifth two Hearst pairs: the structural primitives described further down.
The pipeline produces them in this order, and each is a different kind of result.
Structure, read and parsed by Engine::analyze. Sections, paragraphs, sentences, tokens, and the structural primitive fields. Derived from the parse, checkable against the source bytes.

Measures, filled by Engine::analyze as its last step. Six Option<f64> slots filled by the metric suite: three per paragraph, two per document, plus the materialized passive_ratio. None means not computed, which is distinct from a computed zero.

Outcomes, from free functions over the Document: summarize and keyphrases, with _with forms that name the method. They return Summary and Keyphrases values, each carrying the document's provenance with the method and its parameters, never fields on the tree.

Semantic, with the reference embedder behind the model2vec feature. clusters returns a Clusters value whose provenance carries the embedder's identity and the threshold you supplied. This tier depends on the model, so by design it never becomes a field on Document or Sentence.

A structural primitive is a construction read off the dependency graph and reported as a field. Six of them are computed once and travel with the sentence into every language binding: five at Sentence construction, and hearst_pairs as the engine parses each paragraph, because its detector lives outside the domain (a Sentence built by hand has an empty hearst_pairs). They name an arc shape. They never name a judgment.
Two consequences of reporting arcs rather than readings:

root_mood consults neither negation nor modals. The detector reads the root and its finiteness carriers. Nothing else. The sky is not blue reports Ind and also carries a negation; an indicative root that no modal governs is Ind with no modal whose head_id is the root's id. Combining the facts is your code's job.
Overlap is intentional. never in the example above is both a Negation and a RootAdverbial, because it satisfies both arc shapes. Neither field is assigning it a meaning, so neither has to win.

Passive voice is the seventh construction, a flag rather than a list of arcs: Sentence::passive is true when a token carries nsubj:pass, nsubjpass, or aux:pass, and its document-level share is the passive_ratio field of DocumentMetrics.
Reporting verbs and root adverbials are open word classes, so matra ships no lexicon for either. Sentence::clausal_complements_in and Sentence::root_adverbials_in filter by a list you supply.
Situation model covers what this output is for. Programming model covers the surface that produces it.
